questions.prompt: Why are the contrast rules for large text more forgiving?

options.text: Large text is only used for decorative purposes.
Large, thick letterforms provide more surface area for the eye to track.
Large text cannot be rendered in low-contrast colors.
Users automatically zoom out when reading large text.

questions.explanation: The physical weight and size of large text make it inherently easier to resolve, lowering the need for high contrast.
questions.hint: Think about how physical size impacts how easily the eye catches a shape.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize how physical size impacts visual perception.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum contrast ratio required for text that qualifies as large?
questions.explanation: Large text allows the contrast threshold to drop from 4.5 down to 3.
questions.hint: It is the lower of the two standard thresholds.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify the 3 ratio threshold for large text.

questions.prompt: In Avene, at what pixel size does Bold text count as large?
questions.explanation: Text qualifies as large at 24 pixels in a regular weight, or 18.66 pixels in a bold weight. SemiBold does not count.
questions.hint: Bold text requires slightly fewer pixels to reach the threshold than regular weight text.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Define the specific pixel sizes that qualify text as large.
